claims.summary: When the signed lower bound does not exceed the signed upper bound, every result guaranteed by the exported function lies within those bounds.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi r : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Relational.Lifted.module "clamp"
      [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi] [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 r] →
    lo.sle hi = true → lo.sle r = true ∧ r.sle hi = true
claims.reason: With signed `lo ≤ hi`, the statement requires every returned value to be within both bounds, as intended.
claims.name: Examples.Relational.clampInRange
claims.intent: With `lo ≤ hi` (signed), `clamp(x, lo, hi)` lies in `[lo, hi]`.
details: Covers all 32-bit input bit patterns for the three i32 arguments: the value to clamp and the lower and upper bounds.
The bound condition and result comparisons are signed 32-bit comparisons; the claim requires the lower bound not to exceed the upper bound.
For any result covered by `Returns`, the result must be within both bounds.
`Returns` additionally requires a fresh instance to be instantiable and every call, under every host behavior, to terminate without trapping and return exactly the stated result.
caveats: The guarantee is conditional: it says nothing for calls that do not satisfy `Returns`.
It only guarantees the result lies within the signed bounds; it does not specify how the function chooses that result or that it is the usual clamp of the input.

claims.summary: The unsigned greatest common divisor of any two 32-bit inputs is unchanged when their order is swapped.
claims.statement: ∀ (a b : BitVec 32), a.toNat.gcd b.toNat = b.toNat.gcd a.toNat
claims.reason: The statement says the unsigned gcd is unchanged when the two inputs are swapped, for every pair of inputs.
claims.name: Examples.Relational.gcdComm
claims.intent: The greatest common divisor does not depend on the order of its arguments.
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit bit patterns.
Each input is converted to its unsigned natural-number value before taking the greatest common divisor.
The claim states that swapping the two inputs leaves the greatest common divisor unchanged.
caveats: This is a mathematical identity about the inputs, not a claim about calling a WebAssembly export; it has no termination or no-trap guarantee.

claims.summary: Whenever the exported function returns as specified, its unsigned 32-bit result is no greater than its unsigned 32-bit input.
claims.statement:
∀ (n r : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Relational.Lifted.module "sum_to" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 n] [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 r] →
    r ≤ n
claims.reason: The statement asserts the intended unsigned bound whenever `sum_to` returns. The example at 5 shows the binary violates that assertion, but does not change what the formal claim asserts.
claims.name: Examples.Relational.sumToAtMost
details: Covers every 32-bit input bit pattern for the i32 argument and every 32-bit result.
The result comparison is the ordinary unsigned 32-bit order, not a signed comparison.
For any result covered by `Returns`, the result is no greater than the input in unsigned order.
`Returns` additionally requires a fresh instance to be instantiable and every call, under every host behavior, to terminate without trapping and return exactly the stated result.
caveats: The result bound is unsigned even though the values are 32-bit bit patterns; it does not assert a bound using signed interpretation.
It says nothing about the exact sum or other behavior of the export, and applies only when `Returns` holds.
